headline_marked: Geekom admits to shipping [[malware-laced network drivers]] for AMD mini PCs
headline: Geekom admits to shipping malware-laced network drivers for AMD mini PCs
summary: The company has removed the malicious package and is offering guidance to affected users, but the backdoor malware granted administrator-level permissions.
details: Geekom has confirmed that network drivers for several of its mini-PC models, including the A7, A8, AE7, AE8, AX7 Pro, and AX8 Pro, were found to contain the Asruex backdoor malware. This malicious software could allow attackers to steal data, intercept keystrokes, and retrieve passwords.

The malware was discovered in a driver installer found on a legacy support page for these machines. While Geekom claims this page has been replaced and is no longer accessible through normal navigation, it remained indexed by search engines, potentially exposing many users.

Geekom has since removed the compromised driver package and issued an apology. They are advising users of the affected mini-PCs to perform a full system wipe or at least a Windows Defender offline scan.

The malware granted administrator-level permissions, allowing it to connect to command-and-control centers for remote access. This incident highlights the risks associated with downloading drivers from sources other than official Windows Update or directly from manufacturer support pages, though even those can sometimes be compromised.

This situation is reminiscent of past incidents involving other hardware manufacturers, such as AceMagic and Asus, which also faced issues with malware being distributed through software updates or pre-installed on devices.
